title: Hukum Siber, ITE, dan Ruang Digital (Cyber Law, Electronic Information & Transactions)
description: Panduan komprehensif hukum siber, transaksi elektronik, tindak pidana ITE, tata kelola sistem elektronik, dan pelindungan data pribadi di Indonesia. / A comprehensive guide to Indonesian cyber law, electronic information and transactions, cybercrimes, electronic system governance, and personal data protection.

sections.topic: Kerangka Regulasi dan Evolusi Perundang-undangan ITE (Legislative Framework & Evolution)
sections.content_id:
Landasan hukum siber di Indonesia bertumpu pada Undang-Undang Nomor 11 Tahun 2008 tentang Informasi dan Transaksi Elektronik (UU ITE), yang telah mengalami dua kali pembaruan substansial:

1. UU No. 19 Tahun 2016 (Perubahan Pertama UU ITE): Melakukan penyesuaian ancaman pidana penghinaan/pencemaran nama baik, menyisipkan hak penghapusan informasi elektronik yang tidak relevan (right to be forgotten) melalui penetapan pengadilan, menegaskan kewenangan pemutusan akses (access blocking) oleh pemerintah terhadap konten terlarang, serta memperketat mekanisme intersepsi/penyadapan yang wajib dilakukan dalam koridor hukum penegakan pidana.

2. UU No. 1 Tahun 2024 (Perubahan Kedua UU ITE): Menandai harmonisasi fundamental pasca-pemberlakuan Surat Keputusan Bersama (SKB) Pedoman Kriteria Implementasi UU ITE Tahun 2021. Perubahan kunci meliputi: (a) Pengukuhan pencemaran nama baik (Pasal 27A) secara tegas sebagai delik aduan absolut yang hanya dapat dilaporkan oleh individu korban perseorangan; (b) Pengaturan delik baru mengenai pemberitahuan bohong atau hoaks yang memicu kerusuhan di masyarakat (Pasal 28 ayat 3); (c) Pengaturan kejahatan pemerasan dan pengancaman siber (Pasal 27B); (d) Kewajiban bagi Penyelenggara Sistem Elektronik (PSE) untuk menyelenggarakan pelindungan khusus bagi anak yang mengakses ruang digital (Pasal 16A); serta (e) Pengakuan kontrak elektronik berbahasa asing yang wajib menyertakan terjemahan bahasa Indonesia.

Kerangka siber nasional turut ditopang oleh regulasi pelaksana vital: Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 71 Tahun 2019 tentang Penyelenggaraan Sistem dan Transaksi Elektronik (PP PSTE), Permenkominfo Nomor 5 Tahun 2020 jo. Permenkominfo Nomor 10 Tahun 2021 tentang PSE Lingkup Privat, Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi (UU PDP), serta integrasi delik siber ke dalam Undang-Undang Nomor 1 Tahun 2023 tentang Kitab Undang-Undang Hukum Pidana (KUHP Nasional).
sections.content_en:
The foundation of Indonesian cyber jurisprudence is anchored in Law No. 11 of 2008 on Electronic Information and Transactions (UU ITE), which has undergone two landmark statutory revisions:

1. Law No. 19 of 2016 (First Amendment): Reduced penal sanctions for cyber defamation, codified the judicial right to be forgotten (penghapusan informasi elektronik yang tidak relevan), explicitly authorized governmental access termination (takedown and blocking) against illegal digital content, and tightened procedural safeguards governing lawful telecommunications interception.

2. Law No. 1 of 2024 (Second Amendment): Carried out comprehensive structural harmonization following the 2021 Joint Ministerial Decree (SKB) on ITE Implementation Guidelines. Pivotal legislative reforms include: (a) Reclassifying cyber defamation (Article 27A) strictly as an absolute complaint-based offense (delik aduan absolut) enforceable only by affected individual natural persons; (b) Establishing an autonomous offense for malicious hoaxes inciting palpable public riots or unrest (Article 28 paragraph 3); (c) Codifying distinct offenses for digital extortion and blackmail (Article 27B); (d) Enacting mandatory statutory safeguards obligating Electronic System Providers (PSE) to protect minors accessing online platforms (Article 16A); and (e) Mandating that standard electronic contracts executed in foreign languages must incorporate Indonesian translations.

This statutory architecture is reinforced by pivotal implementing instruments: Government Regulation No. 71 of 2019 on the Provision of Electronic Systems and Transactions (PP PSTE), Minister of Communication and Informatics Regulation No. 5 of 2020 jo. No. 10 of 2021 on Private Scope Electronic System Providers, Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection (UU PDP), and the codification of cyber offenses within Law No. 1 of 2023 on the National Criminal Code (KUHP).

sections.topic: Asas-Asas Hukum Siber dan Yurisdiksi Ekstrateritorial (Legal Principles & Extraterritorial Jurisdiction)
sections.content_id:
Penyelenggaraan sistem informasi dan transaksi elektronik di Indonesia berlandaskan asas-asas universal yang diatur dalam Pasal 3 UU ITE:
1. Asas Kepastian Hukum: Memberikan landasan hukum yang kuat bagi pengakuan bukti elektronik, validitas kontrak digital, dan kepastian hak para pihak di ruang siber.
2. Asas Manfaat: Menjamin bahwa pemanfaatan teknologi informasi memberikan nilai tambah ekonomis, sosial, dan kultural sebesar-besarnya bagi kemakmuran rakyat.
3. Asas Kehati-hatian: Mengharuskan penyelenggara dan pengguna sistem elektronik mengantisipasi risiko kegagalan sistem, ancaman keamanan siber, dan pelanggaran data pribadi.
4. Asas Iktikad Baik: Mewajibkan seluruh pihak dalam transaksi dan interaksi digital bertindak jujur, transparan, dan tidak menyembunyikan informasi cacat tersembunyi.
5. Asas Kebebasan Memilih Teknologi (Netralitas Teknologi): Menjamin bahwa regulasi siber tidak condong atau mendiskriminasi arsitektur perangkat keras atau perangkat lunak tertentu (technological neutrality), sehingga hukum tetap relevan di tengah disrupsi teknologi masa depan.

Dalam dimensi ruang lingkup dan yurisdiksi, Pasal 2 UU ITE memberlakukan asas perpanjangan yurisdiksi atau yurisdiksi ekstrateritorial (extraterritorial jurisdiction). UU ITE berlaku untuk setiap orang yang melakukan perbuatan hukum di dalam maupun di luar wilayah hukum Indonesia, sepanjang perbuatan tersebut:
- Memiliki akibat hukum di wilayah yurisdiksi Republik Indonesia, dan/atau
- Merugikan kepentingan nasional Republik Indonesia.
Prinsip ini menggabungkan doktrin akibat (effects doctrine) dan asas perlindungan kedaulatan (protective principle), yang memungkinkan kepolisian dan pengadilan Indonesia memproses kejahatan siber lintas batas (transnational cybercrime), seperti peretasan infrastruktur kritis Indonesia dari luar negeri atau penipuan daring global yang memangsa warga negara Indonesia.
sections.content_en:
The governance of electronic systems and transactions in Indonesia is governed by foundational doctrines codified under Article 3 of the ITE Law:
1. Principle of Legal Certainty: Establishes solid legal recognition for electronic evidence, digital contract enforceability, and reliable rights allocation in cyberspace.
2. Principle of Benefit: Ensures technological adoption generates maximum socio-economic and cultural dividends for national prosperity.
3. Principle of Prudence: Obligates system operators and users to proactively manage cyber vulnerabilities, data compromise risks, and operational failures.
4. Principle of Good Faith: Imposes duties of honesty, fair dealing, and disclosure of latent system defects upon contracting parties in digital transactions.
5. Principle of Technological Neutrality: Ensures legal rules remain agnostic towards specific software architectures, programming languages, or hardware paradigms, preserving regulatory longevity amidst rapid technological evolution.

Regarding territorial applicability, Article 2 of the ITE Law establishes extraterritorial jurisdiction. The law applies to any natural person or corporate entity committing legal acts either within or beyond the geographical territory of Indonesia, provided that such acts:
- Produce legal consequences within the territorial jurisdiction of the Republic of Indonesia; and/or
- Detrimentally affect the national interests of the Republic of Indonesia.
This framework synthesizes the international legal effects doctrine and the protective principle, vesting Indonesian law enforcement and judicial authorities with competence to pursue transnational cybercrimes, including offshore hacking targeting Indonesian critical infrastructure or overseas electronic fraud schemes victimizing Indonesian residents.

sections.topic: Alat Bukti Elektronik dan Tanda Tangan Elektronik (Electronic Evidence & Digital Signatures)
sections.content_en:
Articles 5(1) and 5(2) of the ITE Law represent a paradigm shift in Indonesian evidentiary procedure by recognizing Electronic Information and/or Electronic Documents, together with their physical printouts, as valid legal evidence. This statutorily broadens the evidentiary categories codified under Article 184 of the Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP), Article 1866 of the Indonesian Civil Code, and Article 100 of the Administrative Court Law (UU PTUN).

Requirements for Legal Validity (Article 6 of the ITE Law):
Electronic Information and Documents are deemed legally valid provided the underlying information remains accessible, displayable, guaranteed in its integrity, and capable of demonstrating accountability and authenticity in elucidating relevant circumstances.

Statutory Exceptions (Article 5 paragraph 4 of the ITE Law):
Electronic evidence admissibility rules do not apply to:
1. Instruments that statutory laws mandate must be executed in physical paper-based form; and
2. Deeds and accompanying documents that statutory laws require to be executed in notarial form or before a Land Conveyance Officer (PPAT).

Electronic Signature Framework (Article 11 ITE Law & PP 71/2019):
An Electronic Signature (TTE) holds binding legal force and evidentiary value if it cumulatively fulfills six statutory criteria:
- Signature creation data uniquely links to the signatory;
- Signature creation data remains under the exclusive control of the signatory during execution;
- Any subsequent alteration to the electronic signature is readily detectable;
- Any subsequent alteration to the associated electronic document is readily detectable;
- Identifiable verification mechanisms exist to establish signatory identity; and
- Means exist to demonstrate the signatory's explicit consent to the underlying electronic document.

Signatures are classified into: (1) Non-Certified Signatures; and (2) Certified Signatures. Certified Signatures must utilize electronic certificates issued by an accredited Electronic Certification Operator (Penyelenggara Sertifikasi Elektronik - PSrE) licensed by the Ministry of Communication and Informatics. Utilizing asymmetric public key infrastructure (PKI) encryption, certified digital signatures enjoy presumptive authenticity and peak probative weight before courts.

sections.topic: Tindak Pidana Konten Ilegal: Kesusilaan, Perjudian Online, dan Pemerasan (Cybercrimes: Decency, Online Gambling, and Extortion)
sections.content_id:
UU ITE menjatuhkan sanksi pidana berat terhadap perbuatan mendistribusikan, mentransmisikan, dan membuat dapat diaksesnya konten terlarang:

1. Pelanggaran Kesusilaan dan Pornografi Daring (Pasal 27 ayat 1 jo. Pasal 45 ayat 1):
Setiap orang yang dengan sengaja dan tanpa hak menyiarkan, mempertunjukkan, mendistribusikan, mentransmisikan, dan/atau membuat dapat diaksesnya Informasi/Dokumen Elektronik bermuatan kesusilaan diancam pidana penjara maksimal 6 tahun dan/atau denda paling banyak Rp 1.000.000.000,00 (satu miliar rupiah).
- Pengecualian Pidana (Pasal 45 ayat 2 UU 1/2024): Tidak dipidana jika perbuatan tersebut dilakukan demi kepentingan umum, pembelaan diri, atau diselenggarakan sebagai karya seni, budaya, olahraga, kesehatan, dan/atau ilmu pengetahuan.

2. Perjudian Online (Pasal 27 ayat 2 jo. Pasal 45 ayat 2):
Setiap orang yang dengan sengaja dan tanpa hak mendistribusikan, mentransmisikan, atau memfasilitasi akses terhadap muatan perjudian dipidana penjara paling lama 10 tahun dan/atau denda paling banyak Rp 10.000.000.000,00 (sepuluh miliar rupiah). Delik ini menjerat rantai ekosistem perjudian digital, termasuk bandar web judi daring, pengembang perangkat lunak taruhan, pemengaruh (influencer/affiliator) yang mempromosikan tautan judi, hingga fasilitator rekening penampung dan gerbang pembayaran (payment gateway).

3. Pemerasan dan Pengancaman Siber (Pasal 27B jo. Pasal 45 ayat 8 & 9 UU No. 1/2024):
- Pasal 27B ayat (1): Setiap orang yang dengan sengaja dan tanpa hak mendistribusikan atau mentransmisikan Informasi/Dokumen Elektronik bermuatan pemerasan dengan ancaman pencemaran atau pembongkaran rahasia untuk menguntungkan diri sendiri atau orang lain dipidana penjara paling lama 6 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 1 miliar.
- Pasal 27B ayat (2): Mengancam korban untuk memberikan barang, memberi utang, atau menghapus piutang dengan ancaman kekerasan dipidana penjara paling lama 6 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 1 miliar.
- Kedua delik pemerasan ini dikualifikasikan sebagai delik aduan.
sections.content_en:
The ITE Law imposes rigorous penal sanctions on parties distributing, transmitting, or facilitating access to illicit digital materials:

1. Cyberpornography and Decency Violations (Article 27 paragraph 1 jo. Article 45 paragraph 1):
Knowingly and unlawfully disseminating, broadcasting, distributing, transmitting, or making accessible electronic materials possessing indecent or obscene content carries a maximum penalty of 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 1,000,000,000.00 (one billion rupiah).
- Statutory Safe Harbor Exceptions (Article 45 paragraph 2 of Law No. 1/2024): Acts are shielded from criminal prosecution if conducted in the public interest, in self-defense, or as legitimate works of art, culture, athletics, healthcare, or scientific study.

2. Online Gambling Operations (Article 27 paragraph 2 jo. Article 45 paragraph 2):
Knowingly and unlawfully distributing, transmitting, or facilitating electronic access to online gambling platforms is punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 10,000,000,000.00 (ten billion rupiah). The offense penalizes the entire operational ecosystem: offshore casino platform operators, gambling software engineers, social media influencers promoting wagering affiliates, and intermediary payment gateway facilitators providing digital escrow services.

3. Digital Extortion and Coercion (Article 27B jo. Article 45 paragraphs 8 & 9 of Law No. 1/2024):
- Article 27B paragraph (1): Distributing or transmitting electronic communications with intent to extort, accompanied by threats of defamation or private secret exposure to unlawfully benefit oneself or third parties, carries up to 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 1 billion.
- Article 27B paragraph (2): Extortionate coercion compelling victims to surrender assets, execute debts, or discharge liabilities under threats of violence carries up to 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 1 billion.
- Both cyber extortion offenses are strictly classified as complaint-based offenses (delik aduan).

sections.topic: Pencemaran Nama Baik, Fitnah, Ujaran Kebencian, dan Hoaks (Defamation, Hate Speech, and Malicious Hoaxes)
sections.content_id:
Revisi kedua UU ITE (UU No. 1 Tahun 2024) merekonstruksi delik kebebasan berpendapat guna mencegah kriminalisasi berlebihan dan multitafsir:

1. Pencemaran Nama Baik dan Menista dengan Tulisan (Pasal 27A jo. Pasal 45 ayat 4):
Setiap orang yang dengan sengaja menyerang kehormatan atau nama baik orang lain dengan menuduhkan suatu hal melalui Sistem Elektronik dengan maksud agar hal tersebut diketahui umum dipidana penjara paling lama 2 tahun dan/atau denda maksimal Rp 400.000.000,00. Jika tuduhan tersebut tidak dapat dibuktikan dan bertentangan dengan fakta yang sebenarnya (fitnah siber), pelaku dipidana penjara maksimal 6 tahun dan/atau denda maksimal Rp 750.000.000,00 (Pasal 45 ayat 6).
- Karakteristik Delik Aduan Absolut: Hanya korban perseorangan (orang perorangan) yang berhak membuat pengaduan tertulis. Korporasi, lembaga pemerintah, perkumpulan masyarakat, atau jabatan profesi tidak memiliki legal standing untuk melapor atas dasar Pasal 27A.
- Pengecualian Kriminalisasi (Pasal 45 ayat 7): Perbuatan tidak dipidana jika dilakukan demi kepentingan umum atau terpaksa untuk membela diri.

2. Ujaran Kebencian Berbasis SARA (Pasal 28 ayat 2 jo. Pasal 45A ayat 2):
Menyebarkan Informasi Elektronik yang ditujukan untuk menimbulkan rasa kebencian atau permusuhan individu dan/atau kelompok masyarakat tertentu berdasarkan suku, agama, ras, dan antargolongan (SARA) diancam pidana penjara paling lama 6 tahun dan/atau denda paling banyak Rp 1.000.000.000,00.

3. Hoaks Penipuan Konsumen (Pasal 28 ayat 1 jo. Pasal 45A ayat 1):
Menyebarkan berita bohong dan menyesatkan yang mengakibatkan kerugian konsumen dalam transaksi elektronik diancam pidana penjara paling lama 6 tahun dan/atau denda hingga Rp 1 miliar.

4. Hoaks yang Menimbulkan Kerusuhan (Pasal 28 ayat 3 jo. Pasal 45A ayat 3 UU 1/2024):
Menyebarkan Informasi Elektronik yang memuat pemberitahuan bohong yang menimbulkan kerusuhan di masyarakat dipidana penjara paling lama 6 tahun dan/atau denda maksimal Rp 1 miliar. Delik ini merupakan delik materiil yang mensyaratkan timbulnya kerusuhan atau kekacauan fisik nyata di ruang publik.

5. Pengancaman Kekerasan Pribadi / Cyberbullying (Pasal 29 jo. Pasal 45B):
Mengirimkan Informasi Elektronik yang berisi ancaman kekerasan atau menakut-nakuti yang ditujukan secara pribadi diancam pidana penjara paling lama 4 tahun dan/atau denda maksimal Rp 750.000.000,00.
sections.content_en:
The second revision of the ITE Law (Law No. 1 of 2024) fundamentally reconstituted digital expression offenses to prevent over-criminalization and protect civil liberties:

1. Cyber Defamation and Libel (Article 27A jo. Article 45 paragraph 4):
Knowingly attacking another individual's honor or reputation by asserting an allegation through an electronic system with intent to expose it to the general public carries a maximum penalty of 2 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 400,000,000.00. If the allegation cannot be substantiated and contradicts factual truth (cyber calumny/fitnah), the penalty escalates to 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 750,000,000.00 (Article 45 paragraph 6).
- Absolute Complaint-Based Offense: Only individual natural persons (human beings) possess statutory standing to lodge a formal complaint. Corporations, government ministries, public institutions, or professional associations cannot file defamation complaints under Article 27A.
- Public Interest & Self-Defense Safe Harbor (Article 45 paragraph 7): The act is strictly immune from penalization if executed for bona fide public interest advocacy or necessary self-defense.

2. Hate Speech Targeting SARA Classes (Article 28 paragraph 2 jo. Article 45A paragraph 2):
Disseminating electronic information purposely designed to incite hatred or hostility against individuals or community groups based on ethnicity, religion, race, and inter-group categories (SARA) is punishable by up to 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 1,000,000,000.00.

3. Deceptive Consumer Fraud (Article 28 paragraph 1 jo. Article 45A paragraph 1):
Disseminating false and misleading electronic information causing direct pecuniary harm to consumers in electronic transactions is punishable by up to 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 1 billion.

4. Malicious Hoaxes Precipitating Public Riots (Article 28 paragraph 3 jo. Article 45A paragraph 3 of Law 1/2024):
Disseminating electronic information containing fabricated news that actively instigates physical civil unrest or public disorder carries up to 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 1 billion. This functions as a material offense requiring proof of actual physical disturbance in society.

5. Cyberstalking & Personal Intimidation (Article 29 jo. Article 45B):
Directly sending electronic communications containing violent threats or fear-inducing intimidation personally targeted at an individual carries a sentence of up to 4 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 750,000,000.00.

sections.topic: Tindak Pidana Serangan Siber: Peretasan, Penyadapan, dan Perusakan Sistem (Cyberattacks: Hacking, Interception, and System Interference)
sections.content_id:
UU ITE mengkriminalisasi tindakan teknis yang merusak kerahasiaan (confidentiality), keutuhan (integrity), dan ketersediaan (availability) sistem elektronik sejalan dengan konvensi internasional kejahatan siber (Budapest Convention on Cybercrime):

1. Akses Ilegal / Hacking (Pasal 30 jo. Pasal 46):
- Mengakses sistem elektronik milik orang lain tanpa hak dengan cara apa pun dipidana penjara maksimal 6 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 600 juta (ayat 1);
- Mengakses dengan melanggar, menerobos, melampaui, atau menjebol sistem pengamanan (cracking/exploiting security controls) dipidana penjara maksimal 7 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 700 juta (ayat 2);
- Mengakses sistem elektronik milik pemerintah dan/atau sistem elektronik strategis berklasifikasi rahasia dipidana penjara maksimal 8 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 800 juta (ayat 3).

2. Penyadapan Ilegal / Illegal Interception (Pasal 31 jo. Pasal 47):
Melakukan intersepsi atau penyadapan atas transmisi Informasi/Dokumen Elektronik non-publik dalam sistem elektronik tertentu dipidana penjara maksimal 10 tahun dan/atau denda maksimal Rp 800 juta. Penyadapan hanya diperbolehkan secara sah apabila dilakukan oleh institusi penegak hukum yang berwenang (KPK, Polri, Kejaksaan, BNN, BIN) sesuai tata cara undang-undang dan penetapan izin ketua pengadilan negeri.

3. Perusakan dan Perubahan Data / Data Interference (Pasal 32 jo. Pasal 48):
- Mengubah, menambah, mengurangi, merusak, menghilangkan, memindahkan, atau menyembunyikan Dokumen Elektronik milik orang lain dipidana penjara 8 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 2 miliar (ayat 1);
- Jika perbuatan tersebut menyebabkan informasi rahasia menjadi terbuka untuk umum, dipidana penjara 9 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 3 miliar (ayat 2);
- Jika perbuatan tersebut menimpa sistem elektronik strategis pemerintah atau membahayakan nyawa orang lain, diancam pidana penjara 10 hingga 12 tahun dan denda hingga Rp 12 miliar (ayat 3).

4. Gangguan Sistem / System Interference, Malware & DDoS (Pasal 33 jo. Pasal 49):
Melakukan tindakan apa pun yang berakibat terganggunya sistem elektronik dan/atau mengakibatkan sistem elektronik menjadi tidak berfungsi sebagaimana mestinya (seperti serangan Distributed Denial of Service / DDoS, penyebaran malware, atau ransomware pengunci server) dipidana penjara paling lama 10 tahun dan/atau denda paling banyak Rp 10.000.000.000,00.

5. Penyalahgunaan Alat Siber / Misuse of Devices (Pasal 34 jo. Pasal 50):
Memproduksi, menjual, mendistribusikan, mengimpor, atau menyediakan perangkat keras atau perangkat lunak komputer, sandi akses, atau kode otorisasi yang dirancang khusus untuk memfasilitasi tindak pidana siber dipidana penjara paling lama 10 tahun dan/atau denda Rp 10 miliar.

6. Pemalsuan Dokumen Elektronik / Phishing & Data Forgery (Pasal 35 jo. Pasal 51):
Memanipulasi, menciptakan, mengubah, atau merusak Informasi Elektronik dengan maksud agar dokumen tersebut dianggap seolah-olah data otentik (seperti situs phishing perbankan palsu atau rekayasa identitas digital) dipidana penjara paling lama 12 tahun dan/atau denda paling banyak Rp 12 miliar.
sections.content_en:
The ITE Law penalizes technical intrusions compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA triad) of electronic systems, aligning with global cybercrime standards established in the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime:

1. Illegal Access and Hacking (Article 30 jo. Article 46):
- Unlawfully accessing another party's electronic system by any means carries up to 6 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 600 million (paragraph 1);
- Accessing by breaching, bypassing, penetrating, or cracking technical security controls carries up to 7 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 700 million (paragraph 2);
- Accessing restricted governmental electronic systems or classified strategic infrastructure carries up to 8 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 800 million (paragraph 3).

2. Illegal Interception and Wiretapping (Article 31 jo. Article 47):
Intercepting, wiretapping, or eavesdropping on non-public electronic information transmissions within or between electronic systems carries up to 10 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 800 million. Interception is lawful solely when conducted by authorized state law enforcement agencies (KPK, Police, Prosecutors, BNN, BIN) pursuant to strict statutory warrants issued by the Chief Judge of the District Court.

3. Data Interference and Tampering (Article 32 jo. Article 48):
- Unlawfully altering, augmenting, deleting, damaging, transferring, or concealing electronic documents belonging to others carries up to 8 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 2 billion (paragraph 1);
- If the tampering causes confidential state or corporate data to be disclosed to the public, penalties increase to 9 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 3 billion (paragraph 2);
- If the tampering affects strategic public electronic systems or endangers human lives, penalties escalate to 10–12 years' imprisonment and fines up to IDR 12 billion (paragraph 3).

4. System Interference, Malware, and DDoS Attacks (Article 33 jo. Article 49):
Perpetrating any intentional action causing an electronic system to malfunction, suffer denial of service, or crash entirely (such as Distributed Denial of Service / DDoS attacks, malicious botnets, and encrypting ransomware campaigns) is punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 10,000,000,000.00.

5. Misuse of Cyber Devices and Exploits (Article 34 jo. Article 50):
Manufacturing, vending, distributing, importing, or provisioning specialized computer hardware, exploit software, keyloggers, passwords, or access credentials designed to facilitate cybercrimes is punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 10 billion.

6. Digital Document Forgery and Phishing (Article 35 jo. Article 51):
Manipulating, generating, or modifying electronic information with intent to deceive recipients into treating it as authentic data (e.g., fraudulent banking phishing pages, spoofed executive identities, forged digital credentials) is punishable by up to 12 years' imprisonment and/or fines up to IDR 12 billion.

sections.topic: Tata Kelola Penyelenggara Sistem Elektronik (PSE) dan Moderasi Konten (PSE Governance & Content Moderation)
sections.content_id:
Penyelenggaraan sistem elektronik di Indonesia diatur secara ketat melalui PP No. 71 Tahun 2019 dan Permenkominfo No. 5 Tahun 2020 jo. Permenkominfo No. 10 Tahun 2021:

1. Klasifikasi dan Kewajiban Pendaftaran PSE:
- PSE Lingkup Publik: Lembaga eksekutif, legislatif, yudikatif, dan instansi negara lainnya yang mengoperasikan sistem elektronik pelayanan publik.
- PSE Lingkup Privat: Badan usaha atau perorangan yang menyelenggarakan sistem digital untuk perdagangan daring (e-commerce), media sosial, mesin pencari, layanan komunikasi, transaksi keuangan, atau pengolahan data pribadi. PSE Privat domestik maupun asing (seperti Meta, Google, Apple, TikTok, Netflix) wajib mendaftarkan sistem elektroniknya kepada Kementerian Kominfo sebelum beroperasi.

2. Kewajiban Moderasi Konten dan Pemutusan Akses (Takedown):
Berdasarkan Pasal 40 UU ITE dan Permenkominfo 5/2020, PSE Privat bertanggung jawab memastikan sistemnya tidak memuat atau memfasilitasi penyebaran Informasi Elektronik Terlarang (pornografi, perjudian online, radikalisme/terorisme, kekerasan, pelanggaran hak cipta, atau konten yang menimbulkan keresahan masyarakat dan mengganggu ketertiban umum).
- Tenggang Waktu Pemutusan Akses: Terhadap konten mendesak (terorisme, pornografi anak, ancaman kedaulatan negara), PSE wajib melakukan pemutusan akses maksimal 1 x 4 jam sejak pemberitahuan resmi Kominfo; terhadap konten terlarang lainnya, batas waktu pemutusan akses adalah 1 x 24 jam.

3. Sanksi Administratif:
PSE yang tidak mendaftar atau lalai mematuhi perintah pemutusan akses dikenai sanksi administratif berjenjang: teguran tertulis, denda administratif, penghentian sementara kegiatan usaha, hingga pemutusan akses teknis permanen (access blocking/pemblokiran DNS & IP) di wilayah Indonesia.

4. Pelindungan Khusus bagi Anak di Ranah Digital (Pasal 16A UU No. 1/2024):
Penyelenggara Sistem Elektronik yang produk atau layanannya ditujukan atau dapat diakses oleh anak wajib:
- Menyediakan batasan umur pengguna yang jelas;
- Memasang mekanisme verifikasi usia yang andal;
- Menyediakan mekanisme pelaporan penyalahgunaan atau kekerasan seksual daring terhadap anak; dan
- Menghapus konten berbahaya yang mengancam keselamatan fisik, mental, dan moral anak.
sections.content_en:
The regulatory supervision of electronic system operators is governed comprehensively by Government Regulation No. 71 of 2019 and Ministerial Regulation No. 5 of 2020 jo. No. 10 of 2021:

1. Taxonomy and Mandatory Registration of PSEs:
- Public Scope PSEs: State executive, legislative, and judicial bodies running digital public administrative services.
- Private Scope PSEs: Corporate entities and individuals offering digital portals for e-commerce, social networking, search engines, financial services, messaging, or cloud data processing. Both domestic and foreign tech conglomerates (e.g., Meta, Google, Apple, TikTok, Netflix) are statutorily required to register their electronic systems with the Ministry of Communication and Informatics prior to commercial launch.

2. Content Moderation Directives and Takedown Obligations:
Pursuant to Article 40 of the ITE Law and Regulation No. 5/2020, Private PSEs must actively ensure their infrastructure neither hosts nor facilitates prohibited electronic information (child sexual exploitation, online gambling, violent extremism, terrorism, copyright infringement, or materials disturbing public peace and security).
- Mandatory Takedown Timelines: For urgent categories (terrorism, child pornography, immediate threats to national sovereignty), platforms must terminate access within an immutable window of 4 hours following formal ministry notification; for other unlawful categories, the takedown deadline is 24 hours.

3. Progressive Administrative Sanctions:
PSEs that fail to register or refuse to execute lawful takedown orders are subject to graduated sanctions: formal written reprimands, administrative fines, temporary operational suspensions, and ultimate nationwide IP/DNS access blocking across all Indonesian telecommunications gateways.

4. Statutory Child Online Protection Mandates (Article 16A of Law No. 1/2024):
Electronic System Providers whose services are directed at or accessible by minors must:
- Implement transparent minimum age criteria;
- Deploy robust age verification technologies;
- Provide responsive reporting channels for child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and cyberbullying; and
- Expeditiously purge algorithmic material detrimental to the moral, psychological, and physical safety of children.

sections.topic: Rezim Pelindungan Data Pribadi (UU PDP No. 27/2022) dan Hak Subjek Data (Personal Data Protection Framework)
Hukum Kontrak Elektronik dan Perlindungan Konsumen Digital (Electronic Contracts & Digital Commerce)
sections.content_id:
Transaksi ekonomi digital di Indonesia diatur secara terpadu melalui KUHPerdata, UU No. 8 Tahun 1999 tentang Perlindungan Konsumen, UU No. 7 Tahun 2014 tentang Perdagangan jo. PP No. 80 Tahun 2019 tentang Perdagangan Melalui Sistem Elektronik (PMSE), serta UU ITE dan PP 71/2019:

1. Syarat Sah Kontrak Elektronik (Pasal 46 & 47 PP 71/2019 jo. Pasal 1320 KUHPerdata):
Transaksi elektronik yang dituangkan dalam Kontrak Elektronik mengikat secara hukum bagi para pihak berdasarkan asas pacta sunt servanda. Kontrak elektronik sah apabila memenuhi 4 syarat:
- Kesepakatan para pihak (dinyatakan melalui klik persetujuan/click-wrap, tanda tangan digital, atau pertukaran data elektronik);
- Kecakapan para pihak untuk melakukan perbuatan hukum;
- Adanya hal tertentu mengenai objek transaksi yang jelas; dan
- Suatu sebab/kausa yang halal dan tidak dilarang oleh undang-undang.

2. Klausula Baku dan Larangan Eksonerasi:
Berdasarkan Pasal 18 UU Perlindungan Konsumen, pelaku usaha digital (e-commerce) dilarang mencantumkan klausula baku yang sepihak mengalihkan tanggung jawab hukum pelaku usaha kepada konsumen (clausula exoneratie), menyatakan bahwa konsumen tunduk pada perubahan syarat sepihak tanpa konfirmasi, atau menghilangkan hak gugat konsumen atas cacat barang/jasa yang diterima.

3. Hak Pembatalan dan Pengembalian Dana (Refund):
Konsumen berhak membatalkan pesanan dan menuntut pengembalian dana penuh atau penggantian barang jika barang/jasa yang dikirimkan tidak sesuai dengan sampel, gambar, atau spesifikasi yang diiklankan, atau terlambat dikirim melebihi batas waktu yang disepakati.

4. Batasan Tanggung Jawab Platform (Safe Harbor Policy):
Surat Edaran Menkominfo Nomor 5 Tahun 2016 mengatur batasan tanggung jawab penyedia platform perdagangan digital (marketplace / user-generated content) atas konten unggahan pedagang pihak ketiga (merchants). Platform dilindungi dari tanggung jawab hukum perdata/pidana atas barang terlarang atau pelanggaran HKI yang diunggah pedagang, sepanjang platform bersikap netral, menyediakan saluran pengaduan pelanggaran, dan segera melakukan tindakan penurunan barang (notice and take down) dalam waktu 1 x 24 jam setelah menerima laporan pengaduan yang sah.
sections.content_en:
Commercial digital transactions in Indonesia are governed through the intersection of the Indonesian Civil Code, Law No. 8 of 1999 on Consumer Protection, Law No. 7 of 2014 on Trade jo. Government Regulation No. 80 of 2019 on Electronic Commerce (PMSE), the ITE Law, and PP 71/2019:

1. Enforceability of Electronic Contracts (Articles 46 & 47 PP 71/2019 jo. Article 1320 Civil Code):
Transactions executed via Electronic Contracts constitute legally binding commitments under the pacta sunt servanda doctrine. An electronic agreement is enforceable if it satisfies four essential elements:
- Mutual consent manifested through verifiable electronic mechanics (e.g., click-wrap acceptance, digital checkouts, certified cryptographic signatures);
- Legal capacity of the contracting entities;
- A definite, ascertainable subject matter; and
- A lawful cause compatible with statutory public policy.

2. Standard Form Contracts and Exoneration Prohibitions:
Pursuant to Article 18 of the Consumer Protection Law, digital merchants and platforms are prohibited from enforcing standard boilerplate clauses that unilaterally disclaim seller liability (exoneration clauses), permit unilateral terms modifications without consumer re-consent, or waive statutory consumer litigation rights for defective merchandise.

3. Consumer Cancellation and Refund Entitlements:
Consumers possess a statutory entitlement to rescind transactions and obtain full refunds or product substitutions whenever supplied goods fail to conform to advertised descriptions, harbor undisclosed latent defects, or breach agreed delivery schedules.

4. Intermediary Safe Harbor Protections:
Circular Letter of the Minister of Communication and Informatics No. 5 of 2016 enshrines safe harbor immunity for digital intermediary hosting providers and e-commerce marketplaces. Intermediary platforms remain shielded from secondary civil or criminal liability for illicit listings or copyright infringements posted by independent third-party merchants, provided the platform acts as a neutral venue, maintains transparent grievance redressal mechanisms, and promptly executes notice-and-takedown procedures within 24 hours of receiving verifiable infringement reports.

sections.topic: Hukum Acara Pidana Siber, Bukti Digital, dan Forensik Digital (Cyber Criminal Procedure & Digital Forensics)
Keamanan Siber Nasional, Infrastruktur Informasi Vital, dan Ketahanan Digital (National Cybersecurity & Critical Infrastructure)
Tantangan Kontemporer: Kecerdasan Buatan (AI), Rekayasa Sosial, dan Kejahatan Finansial Digital (Emerging Challenges: AI Ethics & Cyber Financial Fraud)
sections.content_id:
Lompatan teknologi generasi baru menuntut adaptasi regulasi dan penindakan hukum terhadap bentuk-bentuk kejahatan siber modern:

1. Etika dan Tata Kelola Kecerdasan Buatan (AI):
Melalui Surat Edaran Menteri Komunikasi dan Informatika Nomor 9 Tahun 2023 tentang Etika Kecerdasan Buatan, pemerintah menetapkan prinsip normatif pemanfaatan AI yang mencakup: inklusivitas, keselamatan, keamanan, aksesibilitas, transparansi, kredibilitas, akuntabilitas, dan perlindungan privasi. Penyalahgunaan teknologi AI generatif untuk memproduksi konten deepfake penipuan, manipulasi suara digital (voice cloning), atau disinformasi politik dapat dijerat secara kumulatif menggunakan delik manipulasi dokumen elektronik (Pasal 35 UU ITE) dan penipuan (Pasal 378 KUHP).

2. Modus Rekayasa Sosial (Social Engineering) dan Malware Perbankan:
Kejahatan finansial digital kini marak menggunakan metode sniffing file APK manipulatif (disamarkan sebagai undangan digital atau resi kurir paket), SIM swap fraud, dan phishing kredensial One-Time Password (OTP) untuk membobol rekening perbankan mobile. Terhadap pelaku sindikat, penegak hukum menerapkan konstruksi dakwaan kumulatif-subsider meliputi:
- Akses ilegal terhadap sistem elektronik perbankan (Pasal 30 UU ITE);
- Perusakan dan pemindahan data saldo rekening (Pasal 32 UU ITE);
- Tindak pidana transfer dana ilegal (UU No. 3 Tahun 2011 tentang Transfer Dana); serta
- Tindak Pidana Pencucian Uang (UU No. 8 Tahun 2010 tentang TPPU) guna menelusuri aliran dana dan menyita aset kejahatan (asset recovery).

3. Aset Kripto dan Tindak Pidana Terorganisir:
Pemanfaatan aset kripto sebagai sarana pembayaran tebusan pemerasan ransomware dan penyamaran hasil kejahatan diawasi secara terpadu oleh Bappebti, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK), dan Pusat Pelaporan dan Analisis Transaksi Keuangan (PPATK). Penegakan hukum siber kini mengandalkan teknik forensik blockchain (blockchain analytics) untuk menembus anonimitas dompet digital (unhosted wallets) dan membongkar jejaring pencucian uang kripto.
sections.content_en:
Emerging technological frontiers demand adaptive legal frameworks and specialized prosecutorial strategies to confront sophisticated digital offenses:

1. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Ethics and Governance:
Circular Letter of the Minister of Communication and Informatics No. 9 of 2023 establishes ethical principles governing AI deployment, centering on: inclusivity, safety, technological robustness, accessibility, transparency, credibility, algorithmic accountability, and data privacy. Misuse of generative AI to synthesize deceptive deepfake audiovisuals, cloned executive voices, or targeted political disinformation is prosecuted under cumulative counts of digital document forgery (Article 35 ITE Law) and fraud (Article 378 Indonesian Criminal Code).

2. Social Engineering and Mobile Banking Malware Exploits:
Modern cyber financial syndicates leverage weaponized APK malware droppers (masquerading as package shipping slips or wedding invitations), cellular SIM swap fraud, and real-time One-Time Password (OTP) social engineering to drain digital banking accounts. Prosecutors mount multi-layered indictments combining:
- Illegal access to electronic banking systems (Article 30 ITE Law);
- Unlawful alteration and transmission of balance data (Article 32 ITE Law);
- Unauthorized fund transfers under Law No. 3 of 2011 on Fund Transfers; and
- Money Laundering under Law No. 8 of 2010 (TPPU) to trace, freeze, and repatriate purloined digital assets.

3. Crypto Assets and Syndicated Cyber Extortion:
The exploitation of decentralized cryptocurrencies for ransomware extortion payments and obfuscated dark-web money laundering is tightly monitored by the Commodity Futures Trading Regulatory Agency (Bappebti), Financial Services Authority (OJK), and the Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Center (PPATK). Contemporary cybercrime task forces routinely deploy on-chain blockchain forensics to pierce pseudonymous wallet architectures, trace mixed transactions, and confiscate ill-gotten cryptocurrency proceeds.
